A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support comparison, including matching material relocated or renumbered in v3.

before.justification: v2 reports original molecule/caption generation experiments in Tables 2–5, NLI evaluation results in Figures 4–5, and appendix training analyses and generated examples.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical results and adds model-merging comparisons, weight-ratio experiments and length-conditioned NLI analyses.

M1.justification: The merging, preference-alignment and atomic-NLI pipeline and losses are retained. However, Section 3.2.1 changes the shared interpolation parameter inside the SLERP coefficient expressions to lambda1 and lambda2 without explaining their relationship. Whether this is a notation error or an intended change in weight computation is unresolved.

E1.justification: Both versions use L+M-24 training/validation data and the same separately sampled 3k molecule-caption test pairs for both translation directions. The new long-caption analyses filter this retained test set rather than introduce another dataset, domain or task.

E2.justification: v3 adds model soup as a comparator against SLERP and TIES with CPO for both translation directions (Appendix A, Figure 8). The existing generation baselines and full-NLI, SummaC Conv and SummaC ZS comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: v3 adds a four-ratio merging sweep and NLI evaluations filtered at 50 and 70 words. The stated merging ratio changes from 19:1 in v2 Appendix G, without explicit ordering, to 1:18 (Mol2Cap:Cap2Mol) in v3. This is a reported setting revision; the PDFs do not establish that retained experiments were rerun. Main data sizes, training budgets and metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 substantially expands analyses of both central components: Figure 4 tests the merging-weight tradeoff, Appendix A compares geometric/subspace merging with model soup, and Section 4.2.3/Appendix B test whether atomic-NLI discrimination survives longer captions. These extend v2's existing training analyses and illustrative cases.

E5.justification: Appendix B/Figure 9 newly reports a caption-length mean, standard deviation and fitted distribution. This adds descriptive statistical reporting about inputs, not repeated-run uncertainty. Neither version reports seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals or significance tests for performance.

E6.justification: Tables 2–5 and the original NLI results retain their numerical values, but v3 adds substantial results for merging ratios, model soup and caption-length analyses. Figure 8 reports caption METEOR of 0.65 for model soup versus 0.71 for SLERP and 0.72 for TIES. Atomic-NLI KL divergence is 2.53 on captions of at least 50 words and is displayed as infinite for at least 70 words. These are new subset results, not same-setting improvements over the retained whole-test value of 0.54.

T1.justification: Section 3.2.1 replaces lambda inside the two SLERP sine expressions with lambda1 and lambda2, although those symbols already denote the resulting coefficients. This locally changes the printed mathematical definition and makes it apparently self-referential. The remaining merging equations, losses, NLI definitions and appendix RLHF/HALO mathematics are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion retain the claims about minimal-data merging/alignment and atomic-level NLI evaluation. The added emphasis on 'post-training' clarifies terminology without changing the principal contributions or their scope.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations concerning modality dominance and conflict management, hypothesizes why linear model soup performs worse, and interprets the merging-weight tradeoff. It also characterizes caption dependencies and discusses the new long-caption evidence. The existing limitations concerning static merging, decomposition, domain dependence and generalization remain.

D1.justification: v3 explicitly describes generating MolT5 dispreferred outputs from the 10% training subset, identifies zero-shot evaluation of TxtChem-T5 and Chem-LLM, and specifies layers 0–32 for the merging sweep. Existing QLoRA settings, decomposition/NLI models and data-access information are retained; splitting the configuration display does not introduce new hyperparameter values.

R1.justification: v3 adds Gkoumas (2024) on AlMol and Wortsman et al. (2022) on model soups, connecting alignment to prior work and motivating the added merging comparison. The broader related-work taxonomy and contribution positioning remain stable.

P1.justification: v3 condenses introduction and related-work passages, expands selected methodological explanations, and organizes the experimental setup into Data, Baselines and Evaluation paragraphs. Baseline descriptions move to an appendix, Section 4.2.2 is renamed, and affiliations, contact information and acknowledgements change. Most existing scientific prose and appendix material remain closely matched.

P2.justification: v3 substantially expands the visual presentation with merging-ratio, model-soup, caption-length and long-caption NLI plots. Figure 1 is completely redrawn, Figure 2 is relabelled, and the combined configuration figure becomes three separate displays. Existing result tables, NLI plots, training curves and generated examples are retained, often relocated or renumbered.

improvement.justification: The added model-soup control, merging-weight sweep and long-caption analyses strengthen empirical justification for choices that v2 supported less directly. Clearer experimental disclosures also help reproducibility. These are useful but limited gains, partly offset by the unexplained merging-ratio revision and less clear SLERP coefficient definition; the principal results and claims remain unchanged.
